limits: Illustrative designs only: no data, benchmarks or measured results.
Written for 1990s-2000s relational warehouses (Oracle block splits, ICD-9-CM, CPT-4, HCPCS); standards have since moved on (ICD-10).
Insurance claims processing is deliberately deferred to Chapter 15.
Allocation of costs and weighting factors is conceded to be controversial and arbitrary.
Authors and year are not printed in the chapter extract.
practices: Treat a multi-organisation health care consortium as a value circle: it works only if dimensions (date, patient, responsible party, employer, health plan, payer, provider, treatment, drug, diagnosis, outcome, location) are conformed (p.257).
Choose accumulating snapshot grain for a short-lived bill line item; transaction grain needs roll-forward and periodic snapshot hides current unpaid status (p.259).
Add a companion transaction-grain fact table if users need full detail of messy payments (p.260).
Date foreign keys must be integer surrogates, not date stamps, so 'Not Applicable' can be represented; the date dimension row can hold nulls (p.260-261).
Assign date surrogate keys consecutively in date order and partition the fact table on treatment date key; put special-condition keys at the top of the range (p.261-262).
Do not join seven date keys to one date table; create one view per role with relabelled columns (p.262).
Handle many-valued diagnoses with a diagnosis group key, a bridge table and weighting factors summing to 1.00, rather than multiple slots or a finer grain (p.263-264).
Offer two views over fact plus bridge, one weighted (correctly weighted report) and one unweighted (impact report) (p.264).
If a modelling tool needs PK/FK joins, insert a diagnosis group dimension between fact and bridge (p.264-265).
Reuse a standard portfolio of diagnosis groups in high volume; for hospital stays make groups unique per patient, type 2 SCD, with begin and end date on the bridge (p.265).
Add activity-based cost facts at the same grain for P&L, accepting that allocations are arbitrary (p.265-266).
For complex events, combine role-playing and multivalued dimensions and omit weighting factors on them, giving only impact reports (p.268).
Model sparse heterogeneous records with a fact dimension (entry type) plus generic amount, flag, comment key and file-name columns; return to a classic fact table as density grows (p.269-270).
Keep free text out of the fact table via a comment dimension; storing image file names rather than blobs lets other tools read images but needs a synchronised file store (p.271).
For a late-arriving fact row, choose each dimension row whose date stamp is the latest <= treatment date, swap in surrogate keys, insert into the correct partition (p.272).
Where the warehouse must tie to the books, carry both treatment date and booking date (p.272).
For a late-arriving dimension row, insert a new row, overwrite later rows, repoint fact foreign keys, and fix begin/end dates; non-date surrogate keys must therefore be unordered (p.273).
